sections.title: Growth and range
sections.text: Tacinga saxatilis is a clump-forming cactus native to central Brazil. A taxonomic treatment reports a shrub under about 4 m with flattened stem segments and needle-like spines. This contrasts with the cylindrical stems of T. funalis and the much lower, long-spine-free T. inamoena.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Its flowers range from yellow to orange. The rounded to depressed-rounded fruit changes from brownish green to wine red; the taxonomic comparison does not settle whether it is spineless. The plate's flat pads, orange flower and reddish fruit are consistent with the documented features.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The sources consulted do not verify human edibility or a species-specific toxicity profile. Handle the spines with care.
